headline: Zohran Mamdani Demands Trump Release Illegal Immigrant Shot by ICE Agent, Protests Erupt in Bronx

sources.excerpt: Leading New York Democrats expressed anger and demanded curbs on Immigration and Customs Enforcement violence after a federal officer shot a man driving a car in which his five-year-old son was sitting, sparking fierce protests. At least seven shots were reportedly fired and the man was hit in the neck late on Thursday afternoon as children were coming home from school in the busy Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City. Marble Hill is considered part of Manhattan, but is physically located in the Bronx. Federal authorities on Friday morning identified Oscar Belgal as the man shot, saying he was undocumented, from the Dominican Republic and had a felony record and gang affiliations. Belgal was later booked into the Metropolitan Detention Center, Brooklyn, federal lockup, which is newly being used to detain immigrants, according to his attorneys and a US prosecutor who spoke during a hearing on Friday afternoon. He still has a “bullet in his body” and has not been able to communicate with his family, his attorneys said during the hearing. ICE took Belgal on Thursday from a New York hospital into New Jersey. He reportedly spent the night inside the Elizabeth Contract Detention Facility, a privately run ICE facility, before being brought back into New York and being booked into MDC Brooklyn. Meanwhile, Belgal was able to have only one phone call with lawyers on Friday, his attorney Paige Austin with Make the Road New York said. A New York federal judge on early Friday morning ordered ICE to keep Belgal in the area, after his attorneys filed emergency motions requesting his release. The justice department is likely to argue that Belgal’s transfer into New Jersey took place before the judge’s order, making the order requiring ICE to keep him in the area moot. And Belgal’s attorneys have indicated that they will continue challenging his detention. Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, said Belgal refused to exit his car when approached by federal officers who were trying to arrest him, and then accelerated, struck two ICE vehicles and drove towards other officers. An ICE officer then shot Belgal and Charles said the wound was “superficial”. Footage showed a man in a high-visibility construction vest, possibly with a badge on a lanyard, carrying an assault-style rifle and standing close to Belgal, who is sat on the street, while another officer appears to hold a hand to his neck and shoulder area. New York police officers in uniform shortly afterwards carry the man to an unmarked car and lay him in the back seat, handcuffed behind his back. But Kathy Hochul, New York’s governor, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a New York congresswoman, and Zohran Mamdani, the city’s mayor – all of whom are Democrats – led strong condemnation of ICE’s conduct. Darializa Avila Chevalier, the Democratic New York candidate, rushed to the protests and was knocked over in the chaos as local police and demonstrators clashed. The wounded man was conscious and hospitalized, authorities said. A joint statement from Bronx and Manhattan borough presidents Vanessa L Gibson and Brad Hoylman-Sigal, respectively, said their constituents “stand united in outrage” over Belgal’s shooting. “The frustration, pain, anger and trauma stoked by this incident extends far beyond an individual,” the statement said. Mamdani called the incident “unconscionable” and said on Thursday night that ICE, part of the Department of Homeland Security, had “whisked him away” from the New York-Presbyterian Allen hospital in upper Manhattan. A similar incident occurred in Texas last month after a man was shot by an ICE officer in Austin and despite a bullet lodged in his back was taken by the federal authorities from a local hospital to ICE detention about 140 miles away. Ocasio-Cortez and Mamdani demanded ICE be abolished. Both Hochul and Mamdani spoke to Donald Trump and Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, by phone on Thursday night. “I have been on the phone with President Trump and Secretary Mullin negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful,” Mamdani told a press conference. He demanded from the Trump administration that ICE stop its enforcement actions in New York City. “ICE is rotten to its core,” he said. ICE has been stepping up arrests all year despite withdrawing massed militarized ranks from Minneapolis in January and adopting a more covert approach to enforcement. Both Hochul and Mamdani demanded that ICE cease enforcement operations in New York and the governor said she expressed outrage to the Trump administration on behalf of all New Yorkers. Hochul added that the incident could easily have ended in tragedy. “No child should ever have to experience the terror of gunfire,” she said. The child was being looked after by his family on Friday. The streets where the shooting and protests took place were calm on Friday morning but many residents remained shocked and angry. “Here’s an innocent child that was caught in the crossfire,” said Calvin Hayden, a south Bronx native. “That child could have been killed.” Hayden heard about the shooting the night before and said he was immediately disturbed. He came to Marble Hill, the northernmost part of Manhattan, to see the aftermath. “I don’t believe ICE has any reason or right to be in New York City,” he said, adding he thought New York was already equipped on its own to handle immigration disputes without ICE presence. “There’s a lot of individuals who are not committing crimes and they just want to make a better life for themselves,” he said. Some drivers on 225th Street yelled anti-ICE sentiments as they drove past the scene. Mullin said on Friday morning that the ICE officers involved in the shooting did not know there was a child in the vehicle and defended the agency’s actions. But he pointed out that Belgal would have obviously known the child was in his car when he drove it at officers. The exact sequence of events leading up to the shooting have not yet become clear. Mullin said that Hochul had asked the DHS for a pause on enforcement in New York. “No, we are not putting a pause on enforcement,” he said. Mullin criticized New York’s “sanctuary” policies, which restrict how much city agencies and police cooperate with immigration authorities. Belgal, 28, has prior convictions, was serving five years of probation for felony grand larceny and was also arrested on drug charges in 2025, a case that is still pending, according to the New York police department. “What happened today was an outrage,” Mamdani said late on Thursday, adding: “When ICE agents opened fire, a five-year-old child – a five-year-old child! – was in the back seat of that car. Thank God that child is physically unharmed.” Witnesses told local media they heard the child yelling at the officers after the shooting. At least 20 people have been shot by federal immigration agents under the second Trump administration, as well as a rise in deaths in detention. “ICE is a rogue, lawless and paramilitary surveillance agency. It does not belong in New York City and it should not exist in the United States of America. Abolish ICE,” Ocasio-Cortez said in a statement. The representative also condemned the retail company Target for allowing federal enforcement teams to use its parking lots as staging areas from which to launch arrest operations. Protesters held signs saying: “Jail all killer ICE agents” and “Leave our neighbors alone.” “ICE, get the fuck out of our neighborhood,” shouted Gibson, the Bronx borough president. “I’m angry that we have to be here … We are a working-class community. We don’t deserve this type of treatment from the White House.” She encouraged the crowd to get involved in opposing ICE, saying: “There are more of us than there are of them. I want this to be a moment that we turn into a movement.” Protesters gathered at the hospital where Belgal was taken. The police set up barricades and protesters quickly clashed with officers in a chaotic scene. Demonstrators banged drums and shouted: “Shut it down,” and “ICE out!” as cars driving by honked in support. Standing outside the hospital, Murad Awawdeh, the president of the New York Immigration Coalition, said he wanted to see an independent investigation into the shooting led by New York officials. “The pain that you’re witnessing is people who are witnessing their neighbors, their family members, their friends being ripped away,” he said. ICE has arrested more than 19,500 people in New York and nearly 18,000 in New Jersey during the second Trump administration, mostly Latin American immigrant men without criminal histories, Gothamist reported earlier this week using government data, adding that those totals were more than double the number of such arrests in the last 18 months of the Biden administration.

U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin gave his own account of conversations he and President Trump had with Gov. Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani regarding the ICE shooting in Marble Hill on Thursday night. That account, however, raised more questions than answers. During a press conference Friday morning, Mullin claimed Trump offered to transfer Oscar Bergal, the man whom ICE agents shot just after 4 p.m. on Oct. 8 with a 5-year-old child inside his vehicle during an arrest attempt, into NYPD custody if the city would pursue charges against him. “President Trump actually got involved and said that we would release him to New York’s finest,” Mullin said. “If NYPD wants to take the charges and pursue the charges, we’ll be happy to release him into the custody of NYPD.” Mullin did not specify what charges he was referring to. Mullin claimed he relayed that offer to Mamdani and that the mayor responded, “We will not be detaining him.” Bergal has an existing criminal record in New York. Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said Thursday night that he had been arrested for robbery in 2023 in a case that resulted in a guilty plea to fourth-degree grand larceny and five years’ probation. He also has a pending 2025 case for criminal sale of a controlled substance. But on Friday, Mullin did not specify whether he was referring to either of those cases, potential new charges stemming from Thursday’s confrontation, or something else. City Hall has been asked to respond to Mullin’s account and clarify what Mamdani sought during the calls. Mullin also said Hochul told him New York would be willing to assist federal immigration authorities with “over 100 different criminals” if DHS provided notice. But moments later, Mullin referred to the offer as involving “over 100 different criminal or crimes” and said he had asked Hochul, “What crimes are you willing to help us with?” A person familiar with the call said that Mullin either had misunderstood or misrepresented the governor’s remarks. They said Hochul was referring to more than 100 crimes for which the NYPD can cooperate with federal immigration authorities — not more than 100 specific individuals. Mullin also claimed that when he sought the governor’s assistance, Hochul told him, “Well, right now we need to put a pause on enforcement.” The governor said publicly Thursday night that she had spoken with Trump and Mullin following the Marble Hill shooting and “urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York.” But along with giving what he claims was his side of the story, Mullin lied about Mamdani’s response to the stabbing of an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx on Oct. 2. “Not a word was said by the mayor,” Mullin said at one point, later again accusing Mamdani of being “silent” about the attack. In reality, however, Mamdani visited the wounded detective, Jose Mercedes, and his family at Jacobi Hospital with Tisch on the day of the stabbing. The mayor issued a social media statement after the attack as well. Mamdani and Tisch also canceled a previously scheduled crime statistics briefing that afternoon and visited Mercedes at the hospital. Mercedes was later discharged. The two suspects accused of stabbing Mercedes while stealing a chain from his neck remained at large as of the NYPD’s latest public update earlier this week. Mamdani on Thursday night condemned the Marble Hill shooting as an “outrage,” called for ICE enforcement operations in the city to end and renewed his call to abolish the agency. The shooting prompted protests in Marble Hill and later outside Allen Hospital, where demonstrators clashed with police as Belgal was being treated before being taken away by federal agents. More protests are expected to take place Friday in both Marble Hill and in Foley Square. Mullin, during his Friday press conference, slammed Mamdani’s remarks about the shooting. The Homeland Security secretary — who claimed last month that New York was “crime-ridden,” even though it is on track for historic lows in shootings and murders this year, while threatening to bring more ICE agents in the Big Apple — said the mayor’s words “are dangerous and incite hostility; it doesn’t help.” Mamdani’s public remarks Thursday night did not include any calls for violence against ICE or DHS.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded that President Donald Trump end all ICE enforcement in the state after a federal agent shot an illegal immigrant in the Bronx on Thursday, sparking protests and confrontations with law enforcement. DHS said the man, who was described as an illegal immigrant, had a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests involving assault, robbery, drug possession and weapons possession. The agency also alleged that he had ties to the Trinitarios gang. At a news conference late Thursday night, Mamdani condemned the shooting and said he spoke with Trump for about two hours following the incident. Mamdani said he urged Trump to have the man released — an effort that was unsuccessful — and said New York City wants ICE agents out. "All they do is terrorize this city," the mayor said of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Mamdani also accused ICE of acting "with impunity" and spreading "chaos and terror" across the country, alleging that ICE has killed more people than it has saved. "Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known," the mayor said. "ICE is rotten to its core," he added. Mamdani also confirmed that the man who was shot has been transported out of the hospital by ICE agents. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul also said she spoke to Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. "Tonight, I spoke with President Trump and DHS Secretary Mullin about the shooting in Marble Hill," she said on X. "I expressed outrage on behalf of New Yorkers and urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York. I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth." ICE was attempting to arrest a wanted man from the Dominican Republic at around 4 p.m. on Thursday when an agent opened fire and wounded him, according to DHS, which did not provide details on what led to the shooting. "ICE officers immediately rendered aid. The individual is alive and at a local hospital. The FBI and HSI are on the scene. The incident remains under investigation. More information will be shared as it becomes available," DHS said in a statement. Later Thursday night, New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch identified the man as a 28-year-old and said a 5-year-old boy believed to be his son was inside the vehicle with him during the shooting. "Based on evidence collected at the scene, we know that at least one ICE agent discharged the seven rounds, striking the driver in the neck below his left ear," Tisch said, adding that the boy was not injured and is in the care of a family member. The agency said the man was arrested by New York City police on Dec. 7, 2023, but was released several days later. DHS blamed New York City's sanctuary policies for his release. Hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where the wounded man was being treated, and chanted "ICE off our streets" and "No justice, no peace." Protesters and police were seen shoving one another during the demonstration as officers began to set barricades, and some demonstrators threw water bottles at the officers. "From Palestine to Mexico, all these walls have got to go," the group chanted. Police made some arrests during the demonstration.
